text: Cellifugal [Lat. cella , cell, + fugere , to flee]: Ger. cellulifugal . Fr. cellulifuge ; Ital. cellulifugo . Passing in a direction away from a cell. Said of a nervous impulse with reference to the cells from which the conducting axis cylinders arise. Opposed to cellipetal. There is usually an obvious morphological difference between the cellifugal and the cellipetal processes of a nerve-cell. Cf. NEUROCYTE. ( H.H. )
